protocol.instrument_name: Structured Administration and Supply Arrangement (SASA) - TITLE: Administration of Buprenorphine Depot injection by pharmacists
protocol.instrument_version: SASA 033/1-2023 (page footers and enquiries box: 'Number: 033/1-2023 Date: 13/09/2023')
protocol.effective_date: 13 September 2023 ('Effective from: 13 September 2023'; 'Issued by: ... Date: 13 September 2023')
protocol.legal_basis: Issued by the Chief Executive Officer of Health under Part 6 of the Medicines and Poisons Regulations 2016. (verbatim, '1. Authority', p.1). Conditions also cite: 'Storage and administration are in accordance with Part 9 of the Medicines and Poisons Regulations 2016' (condition j) and 'Record keeping is in accordance with Part 12 of the Medicines and Poisons Regulations 2016' (condition k).
protocol.supervision_model: Document's own terminology: 'This SASA authorises a registered pharmacist trained in the Community Program for Opioid Pharmacotherapy (CPOP) to administer buprenorphine depot injections, when requested by the CPOP prescriber and patient, subject to the criteria and conditions below.' Practitioner: 'Registered pharmacist who has completed approved training in accordance with Appendix 1'. Administration is dependent on the CPOP prescriber: condition d requires 'a current treatment plan in place with the prescriber and pharmacy that outlines consent to administration by the pharmacist and requirements for communication of dosing issues to the prescriber'; condition f requires 'The original prescription has been presented to the pharmacy prior to administration'. The words 'collaborative' and 'autonomous' are not used.
protocol.scope_summary: SASA (4 pages) authorising a registered pharmacist trained in CPOP to administer buprenorphine depot injections when requested by the CPOP prescriber and patient. Approved activity: Administration. Approved medicines: Buprenorphine depot injection. Medical conditions: 'Opioid substitution therapy for the management of opioid dependence.' Conditions a-k cover formulation-specific training, anaphylaxis readiness, authorised CPOP dosing point, current treatment plan, nominated dispensing pharmacy, original prescription presented before administration, consent before each administration, adverse-event reporting to prescriber/TGA, an eight-item clinical record for each administration, and storage/administration (Part 9) and record keeping (Part 12) of the Medicines and Poisons Regulations 2016. Appendix 1 sets training requirements (including CPOP Pharmacist Online Training repeated at a minimum of every 3 years); Appendix 2 sets the approved setting (15 minutes post-administration observation, anaphylaxis kit, staffing). No strength, dose, frequency or quantity is printed.

diagnosis_pathways.name: Buprenorphine depot administration under SASA 033/1-2023 - criteria and conditions sequence

steps.description: Confirm criteria before administration (3. Criteria, plus conditions c, d and e): Practitioner - registered pharmacist who has completed approved training in accordance with Appendix 1; Practice setting - a registered pharmacy in Western Australia that complies with Appendix 2; Approved activity - Administration; Approved medicines - Buprenorphine depot injection; Medical conditions - opioid substitution therapy for the management of opioid dependence. Condition c: the pharmacy is authorised as a dosing point under the CPOP. Condition d: the patient has a current treatment plan in place with the prescriber and pharmacy that outlines consent to administration by the pharmacist and requirements for communication of dosing issues to the prescriber. Condition e: the administering pharmacy is the pharmacy nominated to dispense the medicine on the prescription. Appendix 1: all registered pharmacists administering buprenorphine must have successfully completed (1) an immunisation course provided by Health Education Services Australia (HESA) or an equivalent course provided by an RTO or a university or approved by the Chief Executive Officer of the Department of Health, which provides competency in subcutaneous administration of injections, obtaining informed consent, CPR, diagnosis and management of anaphylaxis, documentation of administration and critical incidents; and (2) Community Program for Opioid Pharmacotherapy (CPOP) Pharmacist Online Training provided by Community Pharmacotherapy Program (CPP), Mental Health Commission (MHC).

gates.criterion: Registered pharmacist with approved training per Appendix 1 (formulation-relevant course plus CPOP Pharmacist Online Training)
Pharmacy is authorised as a dosing point under the CPOP and is the pharmacy nominated to dispense the medicine on the prescription

Patient has a current treatment plan in place with the prescriber and pharmacy outlining consent to administration by the pharmacist and requirements for communication of dosing issues to the prescriber
Request comes from the CPOP prescriber and patient, for opioid substitution therapy for the management of opioid dependence

Practice setting complies with Appendix 2 (space for safe administration, 15 minutes post-administration observation area, hand washing, sharps/clinical waste disposal, in-date complete anaphylaxis response kit, up-to-date written procedures, sufficient staffing)

steps.description: Post-administration monitoring and site readiness (APPENDIX 2 Approved setting): a space where administration of an injection can be safely performed, that ensures patient privacy and confidentiality, permits the patient to lie prone in the event of a severe adverse event or anaphylactic reaction, and offers unhindered access for emergency staff to attend and perform resuscitation procedures; an area suitable for direct visual observation of seated patients, for 15 minutes post administration; hand washing facilities; equipment for disposal of sharps and clinical waste; an in-date, complete anaphylaxis response kit; up-to-date, written procedures covering provision of administration of buprenorphine depot formulations; sufficient staffing, during periods of administration to ensure patient safety in post-administration monitoring and adverse event management.

gates.criterion: Site has an in-date, complete anaphylaxis response kit and is appropriately equipped to treat an anaphylaxic reaction
Area available for direct visual observation of seated patients for 15 minutes post administration, with sufficient staffing for post-administration monitoring and adverse event management

steps.description: Adverse event reporting and clinical record (4. Conditions): condition h - all adverse events during or after administration of the buprenorphine depot must be reported to the prescriber and where appropriate to Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA); condition i - a clinical record must be created detailing each administration for the patient, containing: 1. Patient name and date of birth; 2. Prescriber name; 3. Date of administration; 4. Formulation administered; 5. Dose administered; 6. Site administered; 7. Batch and expiry date of product administered; 8. Name and signature of pharmacist administering; condition k - record keeping is in accordance with Part 12 of the Medicines and Poisons Regulations 2016. Appendix 1: the CPOP Pharmacist Training must be repeated at a minimum of every 3 years; pharmacists must maintain competency in both technical administration and knowledge of the buprenorphine depot being administered through relevant continuing professional development and recency of practice for administration of injections.

gates.criterion: A clinical record containing all eight required items has been created for the administration
All adverse events during or after administration are reported to the prescriber and where appropriate to the TGA
CPOP Pharmacist Online Training repeated at least every 3 years and competency maintained through CPD and recency of practice

treatments.notes: Sole approved medicine under this SASA (Approved medicines: Buprenorphine depot injection, 3. Criteria, p.1). Approved activity: Administration (not supply/prescribing). Indication verbatim (p.1): 'Opioid substitution therapy for the management of opioid dependence.' Administration is 'when requested by the CPOP prescriber and patient, subject to the criteria and conditions below' (p.1). No strength, dose, route, frequency, duration or quantity is printed anywhere in the 4 pages - the dose is administered under the CPOP prescriber's current treatment plan (condition d) and must be recorded per administration ('Dose administered', condition i.5). Appendix 1 (p.3) requires pharmacist competency in 'Subcutaneous administration of injections'; the document does not itself state the route of the buprenorphine depot injection. Before administration the original prescription must be presented (condition f) and written or documented verbal consent obtained (condition g). Each administration requires a clinical record containing patient name and date of birth, prescriber name, date of administration, formulation administered, dose administered, site administered, batch and expiry date, and name and signature of the pharmacist administering (condition i). Storage and administration per Part 9 and record keeping per Part 12 of the Medicines and Poisons Regulations 2016. Dosing detail is deferred to the CPOP clinical guidelines for the use of depot buprenorphine in the treatment of opioid dependence (reference printed at p.2). No first-line ranking is printed; this is the only approved medicine in this instrument.

open_questions.topic: Filename says 'LAIB' but the printed TITLE says 'Buprenorphine Depot injection'
open_questions.observed: Source filename: 'SASA for LAIB administration by CPOP pharmacists.pdf'. Printed title (p.1): 'TITLE: Administration of Buprenorphine Depot injection by pharmacists'. The acronym LAIB (long-acting injectable buprenorphine) does not appear anywhere in the 4 pages.
open_questions.why_unclear: instrument_name transcribes the printed TITLE. Whether LAIB and 'buprenorphine depot injection' denote the same product in CPOP terminology cannot be confirmed from this document (recorded in hugh_to_confirm).

open_questions.topic: No strength, dose, route, frequency, duration or quantity printed
open_questions.observed: Approved medicines: 'Buprenorphine depot injection' (p.1). Condition i.5 requires 'Dose administered' to be recorded but no dose value, strength, volume, administration site, frequency or dosing interval is printed in the SASA.
open_questions.why_unclear: TX-1 strength/dose/route/frequency/duration are blank; dosing sits with the CPOP prescriber's treatment plan and the CPOP clinical guidelines (reference at p.2), which are not reproduced. Appendix 1 requires competency in 'Subcutaneous administration of injections' but the document does not state the route of the product itself.

open_questions.topic: No patient-level exclusion criteria section printed
open_questions.observed: The SASA has '3. Criteria' (practitioner, practice setting, approved activity, approved medicines, medical conditions) and '4. Conditions' (a-k). There is no list of patient contraindications, comorbidities or exclusions.
open_questions.why_unclear: EXC-1 to EXC-3 are derived as the negations of the practitioner/pharmacy/prescription conditions that block administration; no patient-level exclusions could be extracted without inventing them. Combinatorics inferred as any_of across EXC-1..EXC-3 and all_of across INC-1..INC-10 (the conditions are cumulative: 'subject to the criteria and conditions below').

open_questions.observed: No minimum or maximum age appears in the 4 pages; the clinical record must contain the patient's date of birth (condition i.1).
open_questions.why_unclear: age_bounds are null/null with provenance on the criteria page; CPOP age rules, if any, are not in this instrument.

open_questions.observed: The document contains no 'refer', 'urgent' or 'emergency' referral wording. The escalation statements are: adverse events 'must be reported to the prescriber and where appropriate to Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA)' (condition h) and the site's anaphylaxis/emergency-staff requirements (condition b, Appendix 2).
open_questions.why_unclear: referral.routine holds the prescriber/TGA reporting statement and referral.emergency holds the site emergency-response requirement; referral.urgent is empty because no urgent tier is printed.

open_questions.topic: Appendix 1 requires 'An immunisation course' for buprenorphine administration training
open_questions.observed: Appendix 1 (p.3): 'All registered pharmacists administering Buprenorphine in accordance with this SASA must have successfully completed: 1. An immunisation course provided by Health Education Services Australia (HESA) or an equivalent course ... which provides competency in: a. Subcutaneous administration of injections; b. Obtaining informed consent; c. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR); d. Diagnosis and management of anaphylaxis; e. Documentation of administration and critical incidents and 2. Community Program for Opioid Pharmacotherapy (CPOP) Pharmacist Online Training ...'
open_questions.why_unclear: Transcribed as printed; 'immunisation course' may be a copy artifact of the template shared with the vaccines SASA. The required competencies are injection-related, not vaccine-related, but the wording is recorded verbatim rather than corrected.

open_questions.observed: 'the pharmacy where administration is being conducted must be appropriately equipped to treat patients in the event of an anaphylaxic reaction' (condition b, p.1); Appendix 2 (p.4) uses 'anaphylactic reaction'.
open_questions.why_unclear: Both spellings transcribed as printed at their own provenance pages; no clinical difference is implied.

open_questions.topic: Pathway step order is derived from the lettered conditions, not from a printed workflow
open_questions.observed: The SASA presents conditions lettered a-k and two appendices; it does not print an ordered administration workflow.
open_questions.why_unclear: PW-1 order follows the conditions' own temporal wording ('prior to administration', 'prior to each instance', 'during or after administration', '15 minutes post administration'); recorded here so the derived ordering is not mistaken for printed sequence.

open_questions.topic: No notifiable-condition statement beyond adverse-event reporting; no version beyond the SASA number
open_questions.observed: The only notification duty is condition h (prescriber and, where appropriate, TGA). No notifiable disease, AIR or My Health Record requirement appears. Footers print 'SASA 033/1-2023 Effective from: 13 September 2023'; no review or expiry date is printed.
open_questions.why_unclear: notifiable.required is set true solely on the printed adverse-event reporting obligation; instrument_version/effective_date come from the footer and issue block.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm with the CPOP/Mental Health Commission whether 'buprenorphine depot injection' (printed title) and 'LAIB' (filename) are the same product and which product names/brands the module should display.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Instrument naming must match the prescriber's treatment plan and prescription wording before go-live.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Obtain strength, dose, administration site, dosing interval and quantity for buprenorphine depot from the CPOP clinical guidelines and the prescriber's current treatment plan before any dosing rule is encoded - none are printed in the SASA.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: TX-1 has blank strength/dose/route/frequency; a prescribing support module cannot issue administration instructions from the medicine name alone.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm each pharmacist's Appendix 1 training: formulation-relevant approved course plus CPOP Pharmacist Online Training, with the 3-yearly repetition and CPD/recency-of-practice maintenance recorded.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: RF-5/INC-2 make training currency a precondition for every administration; lapse dates must be tracked.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm the pharmacy's CPOP authorisations: authorised as a dosing point under the CPOP (condition c) and nominated on the prescription to dispense the medicine (condition e).
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Two separate hard gates that only the local CPOP arrangement can evidence.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm the local treatment-plan template contains the condition d elements: consent to administration by the pharmacist and requirements for communication of dosing issues to the prescriber.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: INC-6/RF-6 cannot be checked automatically unless the plan's required contents are defined.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm the adverse-event reporting pathway for 'where appropriate to Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA)' - what makes TGA reporting 'appropriate', the timeframe, and whether WAVSS/other reporting also applies.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: The document hedges this obligation ('where appropriate') without criteria or timing, so the escalation rule must be set locally.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm site compliance with Appendix 2 before go-live: privacy/safe-administration space (patient able to lie prone), 15-minute observation area, hand washing, sharps/clinical waste disposal, in-date complete anaphylaxis response kit, written procedures, and sufficient staffing.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: Practice setting compliance (INC-3) is a hard gate that cannot be verified from the document alone.

hugh_to_confirm.item: Confirm what a pharmacist must do when a precondition fails (e.g. original prescription not presented, no consent, no current treatment plan) - the SASA bars administration but names no referral destination or timeframe.
hugh_to_confirm.reason: RF-3, RF-4 and RF-6 are NOT_ELIGIBLE actions derived from 'subject to the conditions'; the operational redirect (contact prescriber, defer dose) is left to local policy.
